newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil reserves down $2 bln so far in April-paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil reserves down $2 bln so far in April-paper.

text.p: Brazil's foreign reserves dropped $2.144 billion in April's first 25 days due to foreign debt interest and premium payments and dollar sales in the floating forex market, a local newspaper said.
Financial daily Gazeta Mercantil, citing unnamed government officials, said Brazil's reserves fell to $56.8 billion from $58.9 billion between April 1 and April 25 .

The paper said government officials expect to reverse the outflow by taking in $541.8 million through the issue of parellel bonds and the sale of a controlling stake in state mining firm Companhia Vale do Rio Doce.
The government has slated for today a privatization auction to sell a 40-45 percent stake in CVRD at a minimum price of $3 billion but the selloff faces a host of legal challenges.
"Reserves are like insurance. They exist to be used," one official was quoted as saying.
"There was no loss, we only use them (reserves) to honor obligations abroad," the official added.
